title: Capability interface on omp
situation: omp's own convention for extension tools (its extension authoring guide): an extension registers each tool with a snake_case name, a label, a description, a parameter schema whose fields are each described, and an approval tier of read, write or exec.
decision: One cratylus omp extension registers each capability as one tool that calls the runtime command and adds no behaviour. The tool's name is the capability's concept anchor; its verbs are the anchors of the concepts they act on; its description states the capability's purpose and when to reach for it; each parameter is declared with a schema and described in the context's words; verbs that only read are declared read, and verbs that append are declared write.
consequences: Cut 6 realizes it for the concept journal first. The cold decode of the interface is an example of that cut.
